correctness.rationale: The Gram kernel follows by differentiating K(z,w)=1/[π(1-z\bar w)^2]; its numerator for b/a=t is exactly (1-zv)^2+2t(z+v)(1-zv)+2t^2(1+2zv). At the excluded boundary v=-1 the polynomial P_t has both roots strictly in the disk for 0<t<sqrt(2), one strictly interior at the boundary threshold, and an interior real root for t>sqrt(2). The argument from positive endpoint signs and C/A<1, followed by root continuity as w=-r approaches -1, proves actual interior Gram zeros for every t>0. The cases b=0 and a=0 are evaluated directly. Exact symbolic polynomial checks were run from the embedded Python source, distinct from the analytic infinite proof.

value.rationale: This supplies a complete if-and-only-if zero-freeness theorem for the natural entire two-dimensional family of constant first-order Bergman jet evaluations. It shows a discontinuity at the ordinary point-evaluation kernel: arbitrarily weak derivative admixture creates off-diagonal zeros. The sharp parameter-dependent boundary root geometry provides an explicit mechanism and explains why model-domain transfer of constant jets is nontrivial.
